```plato

    //==
    // # Marching squares — cell numbering
    //
    // The 2D sibling of marching cubes (`library Voxels`), and numbered to match
    // it. Corners 0-3 are the loop (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1) in (x, y); edge e
    // joins corner e to corner (e + 1) % 4, so edge 0 is the bottom, 1 the right,
    // 2 the top and 3 the left. As in the cubes, a corner bit is set when that
    // corner is BELOW the iso level — outside the extracted region — so case 0 is
    // wholly inside and case 15 wholly outside, and both are uncut.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_squares)

    // The X offset (0 or 1) of cell corner c: corners 1 and 2 are the far side.
    MarchingSquaresCornerOffsetX(c: Integer): Integer
        => (c == 1 || c == 2) ? 1 : 0;
```
